wizard.scheduleDesc: Configure the default backup schedule and execution timeout.
wizard.retentionDesc: Control how long backups are kept and the minimum safety floor.
wizard.workerDesc: CPU and memory limits for backup worker pods spawned by CronJobs.

hint.schedule: Cron expression for new sources without a custom schedule. Example: "0 2 * * *" = daily at 2 AM
hint.timeout: Maximum duration for a single backup run before it's killed. 3600 = 1 hour.
hint.retentionDays: Backups older than this are pruned. 0 = keep forever.
hint.minKeep: Always keep at least this many backups, regardless of retention age.
hint.tempDir: Scratch space for encrypted dumps before upload.
hint.tempDirSize: emptyDir size limit. Increase for large dumps.

label.name: Target Name
label.destinationsHint: Leave all unchecked to fan out to every destination.

hint.jitter: Spread the cron's minute field across an N-minute window per source to avoid fleet-wide thundering herd. Default applies to 0 H * * *-style schedules only; explicit minutes are respected. 0 pins the schedule. Multi-fire (*/15, 0,30) is always left alone.
hint.username: Required for all types except Redis (Redis < 6 has no usernames; ACL usernames came in 6.0)
hint.destinationsHint: Leave all unchecked to fan out to every destination.
hint.verifyIntro: Periodically prove the encrypted dump can be restored. The worker generates a one-shot age keypair, encrypts the run with both the DR recipient and the ephemeral one, then re-streams or restores the artifact before the pod terminates. The DR key is unaffected.
hint.verifyMode: stream-validate is RBAC-free. schema-only / sample / full need the chart's restoreVerification.enableEphemeralPodSpawn=true.
hint.verifyInterval: Go duration. Default 168h (weekly). Worker checks since the last completed verification and skips when not yet due.
hint.verifyImage: Pin the verifier-pod image to match your source DB version. Empty → per-DB-type default.
hint.verifyVolumeSize: emptyDir.sizeLimit on the verifier pod. Defaults: 1Gi schema-only, 5Gi sample, 50Gi full.
hint.analysisIntro: Each toggle controls one safety net. Defaults are on; switch off only for sources where the check produces noise (e.g. an intentionally empty schema-only DB).
hint.analyzer: Off → skip stats collection: no schema-drift / charset-drift / row-count anomaly detection.
hint.emptyDumpCheck: Off → don't fail when a dump appears empty. Use only for legitimately empty schema-only sources.
hint.rowDropThreshold: Anomaly fires when a table shrinks below this fraction of its previous size. 0..1.
hint.sizeDropThreshold: Anomaly fires when the dump shrinks below this fraction of its previous size. 0..1.
hint.compression: gzip is the default. zstd offers 30–50% better compression at similar CPU cost.

verifyMode.full: full (spawn DB, full restore + smoke queries)

hint.knownHosts: Run ssh-keyscan -p <port> -t ed25519,rsa <host> and paste the output here. Required unless 'Skip host-key verification' below is checked.
hint.insecureSkipHostVerify: Accepts ANY host key — vulnerable to MITM. Use only for initial testing; populate Known Hosts for production.
hint.tlsMode: Most NAS firmware (QNAP, Synology) labels this 'FTP with SSL/TLS (explicit)' — pick Explicit. Implicit is the older port-990 variant.
hint.insecureSkipCertVerify: Skips TLS certificate validation. Accept any server cert — vulnerable to MITM. Use only when the NAS ships a self-signed cert you cannot replace.

delete.title: Delete {name}?
delete.warning: This permanently removes the configuration. Existing dumps in storage are kept.

ageKeys.title: Encryption Recipients (age public keys)
ageKeys.intro: Each labeled Secret holds one age recipient. The operator merges them into the worker's AGE_PUBLIC_KEYS env on every reconcile.
ageKeys.noKeysHint: Add at least one age public key so worker pods can encrypt dumps.
ageKeys.name: Name (optional)
ageKeys.removeConfirm: Remove recipient {name}? Worker pods will no longer encrypt to this key. Existing dumps remain decryptable with the corresponding private key.
ageKeys.readOnly: Read-only mode — recipient mutation is disabled.

BackupOverdue.title: Backup Overdue
BackupOverdue.desc: No successful backup in over 36 hours. The scheduled CronJob may not be running, or all destinations are failing.
BackupOverdue.action: Check CronJob status: kubectl get cronjobs -n backup. Look for failed Jobs and check worker pod logs.

BackupDestinationFailing.title: Destination Failing
BackupDestinationFailing.desc: Uploads to this storage destination are failing. The backup may still succeed on other destinations.
BackupDestinationFailing.action: Test destination connectivity via the UI (Destinations → Test). Check credentials, network access, and storage space.

BackupDumpSizeCollapsed.title: Dump Size Collapsed
BackupDumpSizeCollapsed.desc: The dump shrank to less than 50% of the previous size. This could indicate data loss, a truncated dump, or a legitimate large DELETE.
BackupDumpSizeCollapsed.action: Compare row counts in the Verification tab. If unexpected, check the database for missing data.

BackupSchemaChanged.title: Schema Changed
BackupSchemaChanged.desc: Table structure (columns, types) changed since the last backup. Informational — may indicate a migration or unintended drift.
BackupSchemaChanged.action: Review recent database migrations. Compare schema fingerprints in the target detail view.

BackupAnomaliesAppearing.title: Anomalies Detected
BackupAnomaliesAppearing.desc: The analyzer detected anomalies in the backup: unexpected row-count changes, missing tables, or other irregularities.
BackupAnomaliesAppearing.action: Open the target detail view to see specific anomalies. Check if recent application changes explain the differences.

BackupLastRunFailed.title: Last Run Failed
BackupLastRunFailed.desc: The most recent backup run did not produce a usable artifact. The dump, encryption, or upload may have failed.
BackupLastRunFailed.action: Check worker pod logs. Common causes: DB connection timeout, disk full, credential expiry.

BackupSucceeded.title: Backup Succeeded
BackupSucceeded.desc: Heartbeat alert — fires briefly after each successful backup to confirm the pipeline is working.
BackupSucceeded.action: No action needed. This alert auto-resolves after ~2 minutes.

BackupOperatorTestAlert.title: Test Alert
BackupOperatorTestAlert.desc: Test alert sent from the UI to verify the notification pipeline.
BackupOperatorTestAlert.action: No action needed. This alert auto-resolves after 2 minutes.

analysis.subtitle: Which validations are armed for this {dbType} source. "n/a" means the engine doesn't model the concept; "disabled" means an annotation has switched the check off.

row.emptyDumpDescOn: fail when dump rows == 0 vs pre-stats > 0
row.emptyDumpDescOff: fail when encrypted dump < heuristic threshold for source size
row.charsetDriftDesc: flag database character_set or collation changes
row.rowCountDropDesc: fire when a table shrinks below threshold (default 0.5)
row.dumpSizeCollapseDesc: fire when the encrypted dump shrinks below threshold (default 0.5)
row.storageScrubDesc: periodic SHA256 re-hash of stored dump (cluster-wide, opt-in)

banner.localEvaluator: Showing locally evaluated alerts (no for: debounce). Configure alerts.prometheusURL for the canonical Prometheus-based view.
banner.phase2RBAC: Cluster RBAC blocks Phase-2 verification. Saving is allowed, but every backup run will fail with "pods is forbidden" until restoreVerification.enableEphemeralPodSpawn=true is set in the Helm values. To proceed without the RBAC change, pick stream-validate — it is RBAC-free.
banner.alertsLoadFailed: Could not fetch alerts: {error}. The local evaluator may not be initialized yet — wait for the first backup to complete.

consistency.hint: Runs that landed on some destinations but are missing from others, since both destinations started receiving this target. A missing upload is the typical cause — the slow destination silently dropped that backup while the fast one accepted it. Runs older than a destination's onboarding are not flagged.

auditPage.showingMostRecent: Showing the most recent {shown} of {total} events. Older events: kubectl -n <ns> get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp
